Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Mara: There was a rattly hum, yes. It seemed to come from the short duct above the jointer, not from the cabinet. The clear inspection section looked dusty, but I didn't open anything or move a clamp.

Jon: I used the south-bay collector at lunch and it sounded normal. I haven't touched the north one today. The jointer's chip chute was clear when I finished around two, though that doesn't tell us what happened later.

Priya: Could the filter be getting loaded? We had a lot of walnut and MDF on the schedule this week. I can check the maintenance log after my class, but I don't want to reset anything before someone looks at the readings.

Mara: I checked the wall gauge from outside the marked area. It was hovering just under the green band, then climbed back into it when the motor settled. I took a photo at 3:22 and added it to the equipment channel.

Cal: I see the photo. The needle is hard to read at that angle, but the repeated dip is clear. Does anyone know whether the replacement belt we installed last month was the same size as the old one? The note in the cabinet is a little vague.

Rosa: I wrote down the belt number during the change: AX-42. The old one had a shiny edge, and the new one was listed as matching. I can look for the receipt if that helps, but I didn't keep the packaging.

Eli: The motor has also been warmer than usual by the end of the afternoon. I noticed it Tuesday, though the room was crowded and the doors were open, so I wasn't sure it meant anything. I haven't measured the temperature.

Mara: One more detail: the sound changed when I closed the jointer gate, but the airflow still pulsed. I didn't run the machine again to test it. There are fresh shavings beneath the duct seam, mostly fine maple dust.

Jon: I can help inspect the duct joints tomorrow morning before the first class. I have a flashlight and a mirror on my bench. Would someone with the collector training be able to join us? I don't want to guess at the filter housing.

Priya: I can be there at 8:30. The sign-up board shows no one booked in the north bay until ten, so we should have room to look without moving anyone's work. I'll bring the logbook and the pressure readings from last Friday.

Cal: Please also check whether the blast gate is fully open. The handle has been stiff since we cleaned the floor last week, and it sometimes stops just short of the mark. I haven't adjusted it because I don't know if the stop is intentional.

Rosa: I can bring the receipt and the spare filter catalog. The catalog has two versions that look almost identical, one for the older collector and one for the newer cabinet. We should confirm the model plate before ordering anything.

Mara: The model plate says DC-3, serial number 1847. I put that in the equipment notes last winter when we replaced the cord. The north bay also has the small gray separator drum, not the blue one from the sanding room.

Eli: That helps. The maintenance sheet calls this unit DC-3A, but the label on the cabinet might include the suffix on the side panel. Could someone check that tomorrow? I don't want to assume the filter listing is right from the front plate alone.

Priya: I'll check the full label and note the date code, then compare it with the log. Last filter change was marked April 6, but the initials beside it are smudged. The sheet also says “watch pressure after walnut run,” with no follow-up entry.

Jon: Here are the observations I have so far:
1. Pulsing began during maple jointing at about 3:15.
2. The wall gauge dipped below its usual range and then recovered.
3. A rattly hum and fine dust near the short duct were noticed.
4. The collector was left off, and no one has reopened the housing.

Cal: That's a useful list. I can bring the handheld sound meter, although it won't tell us what's happening inside the duct. If we take any readings, let's write down where we stood and whether the other machines were running.

Rosa: Agreed. The sanding-room collector will be in use at nine, so that might affect what we hear in the shared hallway. I'll ask the instructor to keep that in mind if we're comparing sounds, but we shouldn't interrupt their class.

Mara: I put a note on the jointer saying “north collector unavailable; use south bay if trained.” I also told the evening monitor what happened and asked them not to switch it on to see whether it has settled. The note is on the handle, not the emergency stop.

Eli: Thanks. Is the south-bay collector okay for maple offcuts, or is there a reason the jointer was assigned to the north side? I remember we moved a few machines during the duct work, but I don't remember the final arrangement.

Priya: The jointer can use either line, according to the layout posted by the panel. The north line was meant to reduce the long hose run, not because of a special material restriction. I'll bring the layout sheet so we can check it rather than rely on my memory.

Jon: I can meet at 8:30, and I have the original duct sketch from the renovation binder. It shows a reducer near the north-bay branch. The installed duct may have changed since then, so I'll bring the sketch only as a reference.

Cal: One question before tomorrow: does anyone remember a recent change to the gate stops? The maintenance notes mention a handle replacement in February, but there's no detail about how it was set. I can ask the shop lead when they're in.

Rosa: I was there for that replacement. The handle was changed, but I didn't see anyone alter the stop. That was a busy day, though, and I wouldn't swear the gate was adjusted afterward. I'll check my paper notes tonight.

Mara: Appreciate all the help. I can stay for the first half hour tomorrow and show exactly where the sound seemed loudest. I also saved the gauge photo with the time visible, so we can compare it with the log instead of guessing.

Priya: Great. Let's meet by the equipment board, review the notes, and decide what we can safely inspect before touching the unit. If we need the shop lead or a service technician, we can ask them rather than trying to diagnose it from the hallway.

Eli: I'll be there. I'll bring the logbook, and I can check whether the collector has a separate run-time counter. No one should restart it just for a reading; we can figure out what information is available while it's off.

Jon: Sounds good. I'll leave the duct sketch in the binder pocket by the board, not taped to the machine. Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "Mara: quick saturday update from the eastbank birding walk. we had 11 people at the boathouse at 7:10, and the path was dry except for the stretch by the willow gate. cloud cover kept the light soft for most of the morning

Dev: i got there a little after seven, so i missed the first check in. the river was high from thursday's rain, but it hadn't reached the lower bench. there was a lot of mud around the map board

Lina: the first bird we logged was a song sparrow near the bike rack. it kept singing from the same low branch while people were arriving, then flew into the reeds when a jogger passed

Owen: i counted three great blue herons along the far bank, not all at once. one was near the footbridge, and the other two were farther south by the old stone wall. hard to tell if they were the same birds moving around

Mara: we also heard a barred owl from the cemetery side at about 7:35. nobody saw it, and the call was brief, maybe two rounds. that area is outside the park boundary but still audible from the path

Priya: thanks for noting that. i had the Merlin app open and got a match for barred owl, but i wouldn't count that as a visual sighting. the app was slow to load with the weak signal near the river

Cal: the kingfisher was back at the footbridge, or at least one was there. it perched on the railing for maybe a minute, then went downstream. i saw it dive once but didn't see whether it caught anything

Dev: quick note on access: the north gate was unlocked when i arrived, and the small gravel lot had room for four cars. the water fountain by the playground is still covered, so bring bottles if you're coming next week

Lina: i found two mallards with ducklings in the inlet beside the community garden. i counted five ducklings, though they kept vanishing behind the grass. please give that corner plenty of space if you walk through

Owen: there were also cedar waxwings in the crabapple trees on Mercer Street. i saw a flock of around 14, but they moved before anyone else got a clear count. one of them had a berry and dropped it on the sidewalk

Mara: for the shared log, i have these as the main notes
1. song sparrow at the east bike rack, singing at 7:12
2. barred owl heard from cemetery side, not seen
3. kingfisher at the footbridge railing, then downstream
if i missed something important, add it here before tonight

Cal: i noticed a red-tailed hawk circling above the water tower around 8:05. it was high up and only stayed in view for a few seconds, so i didn't get a good look at the tail. could've been a hawk, but red-tail is my best guess

Priya: that sounds fair. i saw a hawk over the school field last month, but i can't say it was the same one. the field wasn't part of saturday's route, and i didn't log anything from there this time

Dev: on the walk back, the maintenance crew had put a cone near the cracked paving stone by the south steps. the stone is still uneven, so watch your footing there. nobody from our group used the ramp by the boathouse

Lina: the community garden volunteers were watering beds when we passed at 8:20. one of them asked whether we were looking for the nesting box near the shed. we said we were checking the riverside trail, not the garden boxes

Eli: i spoke with Jo from the garden group after everyone left. Jo said the box had been checked on friday and there wasn't a nest in it. i didn't ask what species they usually get there

Mara: small correction to my first note, we had 12 people total, not 11. Ben joined by the bridge and didn't make it to the boathouse check in. sorry, i noticed his name missing when i looked at the sign-up sheet

Owen: no worries, and thanks for fixing it. the group stayed together until the garden inlet, then split into two pairs for the last stretch. we met back at the south steps just before nine

Priya: for next saturday, forecast says light rain before sunrise and cloudy after eight. that's just the forecast as of this morning, so check again before heading out. the route is still listed as the river loop on the calendar

Cal: i can bring the spare binoculars next week. the left eyecup is loose, though, so i'll put a note on the case. they're fine to use if you keep the cup from turning while you focus

Lina: i'll bring the printed map with the garden boundary marked. a couple people asked where the park ends by Mercer Street, and the online map labels that path differently from the sign at the south steps

Dev: does anyone have the exact time we passed the herons? i wrote 7:50 in my notebook, but that was after we crossed the footbridge and may be a few minutes late. i don't want to make it sound more exact than it was

Mara: i'll put approximately 7:45 to 7:55 in the log. thanks everyone for the notes and for keeping space around the ducklings. i'll post the final list after i check the times against the photos", "output": "Mara: Quick Saturday update from the Eastbank birding walk. We had 11 people at the boathouse at 7:10, and the path was dry except for the stretch by the willow gate. Cloud cover kept the light soft for most of the morning.

Dev: I got there a little after seven, so I missed the first check-in. The river was high from Thursday's rain, but it hadn't reached the lower bench. There was a lot of mud around the map board.

Lina: The first bird we logged was a song sparrow near the bike rack. It kept singing from the same low branch while people were arriving, then flew into the reeds when a jogger passed.

Owen: I counted three great blue herons along the far bank, not all at once. One was near the footbridge, and the other two were farther south by the old stone wall. Hard to tell if they were the same birds moving around.

Mara: We also heard a barred owl from the cemetery side at about 7:35. Nobody saw it, and the call was brief, maybe two rounds. That area is outside the park boundary but still audible from the path.

Priya: Thanks for noting that. I had the Merlin app open and got a match for barred owl, but I wouldn't count that as a visual sighting. The app was slow to load with the weak signal near the river.

Cal: The kingfisher was back at the footbridge, or at least one was there. It perched on the railing for maybe a minute, then went downstream. I saw it dive once but didn't see whether it caught anything.

Dev: Quick note on access: The north gate was unlocked when I arrived, and the small gravel lot had room for four cars. The water fountain by the playground is still covered, so bring bottles if you're coming next week.

Lina: I found two mallards with ducklings in the inlet beside the community garden. I counted five ducklings, though they kept vanishing behind the grass. Please give that corner plenty of space if you walk through.

Owen: There were also cedar waxwings in the crabapple trees on Mercer Street. I saw a flock of around 14, but they moved before anyone else got a clear count. One of them had a berry and dropped it on the sidewalk.

Mara: For the shared log, I have these as the main notes:
1. Song sparrow at the east bike rack, singing at 7:12.
2. Barred owl heard from the cemetery side, not seen.
3. Kingfisher at the footbridge railing, then downstream.
If I missed something important, add it here before tonight.

Cal: I noticed a red-tailed hawk circling above the water tower around 8:05. It was high up and only stayed in view for a few seconds, so I didn't get a good look at the tail. Could've been a hawk, but red-tail is my best guess.

Priya: That sounds fair. I saw a hawk over the school field last month, but I can't say it was the same one. The field wasn't part of Saturday's route, and I didn't log anything from there this time.

Dev: On the walk back, the maintenance crew had put a cone near the cracked paving stone by the south steps. The stone is still uneven, so watch your footing there. Nobody from our group used the ramp by the boathouse.

Lina: The community garden volunteers were watering beds when we passed at 8:20. One of them asked whether we were looking for the nesting box near the shed. We said we were checking the riverside trail, not the garden boxes.

Eli: I spoke with Jo from the garden group after everyone left. Jo said the box had been checked on Friday and there wasn't a nest in it. I didn't ask what species they usually get there.

Mara: Small correction to my first note: We had 12 people total, not 11. Ben joined by the bridge and didn't make it to the boathouse check-in. Sorry, I noticed his name missing when I looked at the sign-up sheet.

Owen: No worries, and thanks for fixing it. The group stayed together until the garden inlet, then split into two pairs for the last stretch. We met back at the south steps just before nine.

Priya: For next Saturday, the forecast says light rain before sunrise and cloudy after eight. That's just the forecast as of this morning, so check again before heading out. The route is still listed as the river loop on the calendar.

Cal: I can bring the spare binoculars next week. The left eyecup is loose, though, so I'll put a note on the case. They're fine to use if you keep the cup from turning while you focus.

Lina: I'll bring the printed map with the garden boundary marked. A couple of people asked where the park ends by Mercer Street, and the online map labels that path differently from the sign at the south steps.

Dev: Does anyone have the exact time we passed the herons? I wrote 7:50 in my notebook, but that was after we crossed the footbridge and may be a few minutes late. I don't want to make it sound more exact than it was.

Mara: I'll put approximately 7:45 to 7:55 in the log. Thanks, everyone, for the notes and for keeping space around the ducklings. I'll post the final list after I check the times against the photos."}, {"id": "arka-v3-train-slack-0032", "row_sha256": "674819d7f354709312495abd9f53e695b259062091d705ca3a0a85a3acff85f0", "mode": "/slack", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Fix grammar, punctuation, and shorthand with minimal edits.
